sources.title: The profitability of technical trading rules in the Bitcoin market
sources.claim: Among seven trend-following families, trading-range breakout showed significant forecasting power and stronger Sharpe performance, especially in strongly trending regimes.
sources.limitations: Historical daily Bitcoin; must clear current BingX perpetual costs.

sources.title: Are simple technical trading rules profitable in bitcoin markets?
sources.claim: Large-scale testing with transaction costs and multiple-hypothesis controls found selected technical-rule portfolios can outperform buy-and-hold out of sample, supporting cost-first screening instead of indicator folklore.
sources.limitations: Rule universe and venue differ from BingX perpetuals.

sources.title: Technical trading and cryptocurrencies
sources.claim: Nearly 15,000 technical rules across five main classes showed predictability/profitability across several cryptocurrencies, motivating systematic primitive extraction rather than single-indicator invention.
sources.limitations: Historical crypto spot markets; current costs and robustness must be revalidated.

sources.title: Intraday return predictability in the cryptocurrency markets: Momentum, reversal, or both
sources.claim: Momentum and reversal coexist, with sign and economic value changing across jumps, liquidity, macro-event and market states; regime ownership is therefore a causal requirement.
sources.limitations: Historical multi-exchange data; no direct BingX execution proof.

sources.title: The intraday dynamics and intraday price discovery of bitcoin
sources.claim: London-New York overlapping hours dominate Bitcoin price discovery and coincide with elevated volume, volatility and liquidity.
sources.limitations: Spot price-discovery study; session edge must be replayed on perpetuals.

sources.title: Time-of-day periodicities of trading volume and volatility in Bitcoin exchange: Does the stock market matter?
sources.claim: Bitcoin volume and volatility are materially higher during US/European daytime and weekdays than weekends, supporting deterministic session and weekday conditioning.
sources.limitations: Bitstamp historical data; conditioning is hypothesis-only until local replay.

sources.title: Up or down? Short-term reversal, momentum, and liquidity effects in cryptocurrency markets
sources.claim: Short-term reversal is concentrated in illiquid cryptoassets, while the largest and most tradeable coins exhibit daily momentum; liquidity can flip the expected direction of the same return signal.
sources.limitations: Cross-sectional study; BTC/ETH implementation needs time-series adaptation.

sources.title: Perpetual Futures and Basis Risk: Evidence from Cryptocurrency
sources.claim: Constrained arbitrage capital and speculative demand create persistent futures-basis dislocations; funding is part of the correction mechanism rather than a standalone threshold signal.

sources.title: Anatomy of Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures Returns
sources.claim: A broad set of basis, momentum, liquidity, size and volatility predictors yields many significant perpetual-futures return sorts; log-basis and a price-volume factor explain much of the structure.
sources.limitations: Recent working paper; replication and source lineage required before use.

sources.title: Funding Rate Mechanism in Perpetual Futures
sources.claim: Funding feedback can induce mean-reverting basis dynamics, while update intervals, caps and jump/liquidation states alter the path and tail behavior.
sources.limitations: Model-based 2026 working paper; local empirical replay mandatory.

sources.claim: Order-flow and volume context can be used as an entry-selectivity hypothesis.
sources.limitations: Hypothesis only; popularity is not economic proof.
